title: Can my own runs predict my 70.3 run pace?
text:
TipKey finding



The model was off by about 41 sec/mile on runs from its own training period. On 12 new runs it missed by 1:09/mile, and it guessed too fast on 10 of 12. It assumed I’d keep getting faster, and a knee injury and new swim and bike training said otherwise.

title: Can my own runs predict my 70.3 run pace?
text:
The question
I’m racing my first Ironman 70.3 on July 18, 2027. Can I predict my half-marathon pace from my own training data?

title: Can my own runs predict my 70.3 run pace?
text:
The data

179 runs from Strava, April 2025 to October 12, 2026, all before I started triathlon training (96 treadmill, 83 outside)
Test set: 12 runs logged on COROS since October 13, 2026, during knee rehab
Target: average pace in minutes per mile

title: Can my own runs predict my 70.3 run pace?
text:
The model
A linear regression with six features: distance, average heart rate, treadmill vs outside, elevation gain per mile, trail runs, and weeks of training (a fitness trend).


Full model code
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 70.3 run pace model: train on pre-triathlon runs, test on new ones
# Uses strava_runs_clean.csv (the output of strava_filter_1.R)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)

runs <- read_csv("strava_runs_clean.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    elev_pm = elev_ft / miles,                                     # feet of climb per mile
    weeks   = as.numeric(day - as_date("2025-04-28")) / 7,         # fitness trend
    trail   = as.integer(str_detect(name, regex("trail|wildwood|ultra", ignore_case = TRUE)))
  )

# 1. Fit the model ----------------------------------------------
fit <- lm(pace ~ miles + avg_hr + treadmill + elev_pm + weeks + trail, data = runs)
summary(fit)
# Per-mile effects, in seconds:
round(coef(fit)[-1] * 60, 1)   # avg_hr x10 = ~23 s faster, weeks x4.35 = ~8 s/month faster

# 2. 5-fold cross-validated error on the training runs ----------
set.seed(1)
folds <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(runs)))
cv_err <- map_dbl(1:5, function(k) {
  m <- lm(formula(fit), data = runs[folds != k, ])
  mean(abs(predict(m, runs[folds == k, ]) - runs$pace[folds == k]))
})
mean(cv_err) * 60   # ~41 sec per mile (random fold split, so yours may differ slightly)

# 3. Test on the 12 runs since Oct 13 (from COROS) ---------------
test <- tribble(
  ~day,         ~km,   ~sec,          ~avg_hr, ~treadmill, ~elev_m,
  "2026-10-14", 4.83,  24*60 + 10,    140,     1,          0,
  "2026-10-16", 11.28, 63*60 + 45,    154,     1,          0,
  "2026-10-20", 6.20,  35*60,         158,     1,          0,
  "2026-10-22", 3.28,  17*60 + 20,    141,     1,          0,
  "2026-10-25", 5.41,  30*60 + 6,     152,     1,          0,
  "2026-10-27", 3.50,  20*60 + 6,     141,     1,          0,
  "2026-10-27", 3.56,  20*60,         150,     0,          48,
  "2026-11-01", 9.83,  74*60 + 11,    129,     0,          121,
  "2026-11-10", 3.04,  17*60 + 52,    145,     1,          0,
  "2026-11-11", 5.08,  38*60 + 28,    124,     1,          0,
  "2026-11-15", 3.91,  23*60 + 22,    144,     0,          34,
  "2026-11-17", 3.62,  21*60 + 1,     149,     1,          0
) %>%
  mutate(
    day     = as_date(day),
    miles   = km / 1.609344,
    pace    = (sec / 60) / miles,
    elev_pm = elev_m * 3.28084 / miles,
    weeks   = as.numeric(day - as_date("2025-04-28")) / 7,
    trail   = 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(pred = predict(fit, newdata = .), miss_s = (pace - pred) * 60)

test %>% select(day, miles, avg_hr, pace, pred, miss_s)
mean(abs(test$miss_s))   # ~69 sec: average miss
sum(test$miss_s > 0)     # 10 of 12 guessed too fast

# 4. 70.3 projection: 13.1 mi outside at 150 bpm, "if I raced today" ---
race <- tibble(miles = 13.1, avg_hr = 150, treadmill = 0,
               elev_pm = median(runs$elev_pm[runs$treadmill == 0 & runs$trail == 0 & runs$miles >= 8]),
               weeks = as.numeric(as_date("2026-11-23") - as_date("2025-04-28")) / 7, trail = 0)
predict(fit, race)       # ~8.58 min/mi = 8:35

title: Can my own runs predict my 70.3 run pace?
text:
The test



Predicted vs actual pace on 12 runs the model never saw


Why it missed:

It assumed I’d keep getting faster. The training-weeks trend only ever went one way in my data.
Then life changed. Knee rehab plus swimming and cycling, none of which the training data had seen.
Some runs were easy on purpose. My two 12:00/mile runs were planned recovery runs, and the model can’t read my training plan.

title: Can my own runs predict my 70.3 run pace?
text:
My 70.3 prediction
For 13.1 miles outside at 150 bpm, the model says 8:35/mile. Adding back its recent miss gives a realistic range of 9:15–9:35/mile. It still knows nothing about running off the bike.

title: Predicting the Las Vegas GP podium
text:
The question
I went to the Las Vegas Grand Prix in 2025 as a fan. This year I wanted to see if a model could call the podium before the race.

title: Predicting the Las Vegas GP podium
text:
The data
All 20 Grands Prix of the 2026 season, pulled into R with the f1dataR package: 440 driver-race rows. I used only 2026 because the cars run under brand-new regulations this year, so older seasons describe different cars.
